$comment: THE redirect map. Single source of truth for cutover (AC-7.1, AC-7.2).
`npm run redirects:generate` reads this file and writes the host-specific redirect
files. Never hand-edit those outputs — edit here and regenerate, or the two will
drift and the drift will only surface as lost rankings weeks after launch.
`npm run redirects:verify -- --base https://DOMAIN` hits every `from` live and asserts
a single-hop 301 to a 200. Run it against staging before DNS, and against production
STATUS: `pages` is now populated from the LIVE site's own Yoast sitemap
(apexgetsitdone.com/page-sitemap.xml, crawled 2026-07-29). That is the whole indexable
surface: 7 URLs. No Search Console or GA4 access was needed for this part, so the map is
no longer empty and no longer blocked on D-01 for its main body.
WHAT IS STILL MISSING, and why D-01 still matters: a sitemap lists what the CMS believes
exists. It does NOT list orphaned URLs that still rank — old WordPress ?p= permalinks,
attachment pages, category/tag archives, or anything unlinked but indexed. Those only
surface in Search Console and GA4. Expect a handful; add them as rows when access lands.
